model: Sum-of-parts: owner-FCF DCF of the Fee Income-related Business plus Real Estate Investment Business at haircut book (engine route with equity_bridge)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: H1 2026 interim note 17(b) weighted diluted count 5,061,572k (4,991,277k basic + 64,909k PSP + 5,386k RSP). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR note 36 segment table, share-based expenses S$39m (FRB 22, REIB 3, Corporate 14); no separate net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0). The fee-business flows carry FRB + Corporate SBC (S$36m, 3.0% of FRB revenue); REIB's S$3m is inside the book-value leg.
inputs.wacc_rationale: SGD-built: Singapore 10y SGS ~2.4%, ERP 5.5%, unlevered beta ~1.05 for a fee-earning real-estate manager -> ~8.2%, rounded to 8.5% for APAC/China fee concentration. Same WACC in every scenario; risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities S$498m (73 current + 425 non-current, 30-Jun-2026) are in total_debt/net_debt; lease principal (S$74m FY2025) is NOT deducted from the flows; ROU renewal is charged through the capex line (capex 5.0% vs D&A 4.0%).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI S$898m (30-Jun-2026) deducted once in the equity_bridge. NCI sits almost entirely in consolidated REIB vehicles whose investment properties are added at 100%; FRB flows are attributable (FY2025 FRB NCI share immaterial). No perpetual securities outstanding at 30-Jun-2026.
inputs.notes: MODEL: CLI is an asset-light real-estate investment manager with a S$18bn balance-sheet investment book, so neither a pure owner-FCF DCF nor a REIT AFFO capitalisation fits; it straddles two routing rows and is valued as a sum of parts per dcf-methods SKILL.md. Leg 1 (FRB: listed/private funds, lodging and commercial management) is an owner-FCF component DCF on FRB segment revenue (FY2025 S$1,208m = FRR). FY0 pre-SBC EBITDA margin 36.1% = (FRB EBITDA 432 + Corporate -14 + SBC 36 - corporate interest income 18) / 1,208. Leg 2 (REIB: associates incl. sponsor REIT stakes, JVs, investment properties) is taken at haircut book in the equity_bridge; its income (REIB EBITDA S$317m FY2025, incl. equity-accounted share of associates) is excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule). Consolidated net debt incl. leases is deducted once. DATA BREAK: Metrics.csv FY2016-FY2019 are predecessor CapitaLand Limited (developer, ~S$6bn revenue) and FY2020 is blank; only FY2021+ is used for any growth, margin or multiple. Consolidated revenue FY2024->FY2025 also falls 24% on the Dec-2024 CLAS deconsolidation, which is why the projection runs on FRB revenue, not consolidated revenue. TICKER COLLISION: the folder is C09.SI but Yahoo C09.SI is City Developments Limited (CDL, ~S$7.13); CapitaLand Investment trades as 9CI.SI on SGX. current_price is 9CI.SI. last_fcf is consolidated owner FCF (reported 479 - SBC 39; interest income not stripped because the group is net debt) and is informational only -- the engine projects from base_revenue. Buybacks S$7m FY2025 (S$358m FY2024), so the flat count is partly funded.

equity_bridge.item: Associates at 0.90x book (listed sponsor REIT stakes near NAV; China/private funds below)
Investment properties at 0.85x book (recent China divestments 13-20% below book)
Other non-current assets (financial assets/fund investments) at book
Development properties for sale at book

historical_growth.basis: Current entity only, FY2021-FY2025 (4 annual intervals). Pre-2021 predecessor rows excluded; FY2020 blank.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (-6%), EPS (-46%) and consolidated revenue (-10%) CAGRs are not growth signals: they reflect the CLAS deconsolidation (Dec-2024), the FY2024 distribution-in-specie of CICT units, China revaluation losses and asset recycling. The fee business (FRR +6.3%/yr, FRB revenue +18% in H1 2026) is the series projected. Equity CAGR diverges >30% from revenue -- flagged.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC): FY2021 567, FY2022 511, FY2023 604, FY2024 518, FY2025 440 -- consolidated, so it mixes fee and investment cash flows and falls as REIB shrinks. SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR tracks reported FCF CAGR closely (SBC ~1.5-3% of revenue).

base.narrative: FUM compounds toward ~S$170-180bn by 2030 (short of the S$200bn-by-2028 target) at a stable ~85bps all-in FRR/FUM; FY2026 FRB revenue +12% after H1's +18% (which carried an India performance fee and event-driven fees); margins drift up 1.4pp as private funds and Ascott scale.

bull.narrative: S$200bn FUM is reached around 2028-29, Ascott hits S$500m fees, C-REITs become a repeatable recycling channel and private funds reach listed-funds margins (~47%), lifting FRB margin toward 44%.

bear.narrative: Event-driven and performance fees revert after H1 2026, private fundraising stalls again, China fund FUM keeps rolling off at end of investment periods, and growth spend on private funds/lodging keeps margins below FY2024's 37%.

scenario_narratives.base: CLI's fee franchise keeps compounding at high single digits as listed REIT acquisitions, private funds (SCCP, Wingate) and Ascott's signed pipeline convert to FUM and fees, but the S$200bn FUM target slips a couple of years. The REIB book is recycled at roughly 10-15% below carrying value (China weighted), proceeds pay down debt rather than creating new value. Fee business EV of ~S$7bn plus the haircut investment book less S$6.6bn net debt and NCI.
scenario_narratives.bull: The asset-light pivot lands: S$200bn FUM by ~2029, >S$1bn operating earnings around 2030, Ascott to S$500m fees, and China C-REIT listings let CLI exit China balance-sheet assets near book. FRB margins scale toward listed-funds levels (~44%). Investment book still valued at the same haircut book (bridge is common to all scenarios), so bull upside is understated if sponsor REIT stakes re-rate above NAV.
scenario_narratives.bear: APAC real-estate capital raising stalls again and China keeps bleeding: FRB growth slows to ~3%, event fees from the H1 2026 divestment wave do not repeat, and margins stay around 34-35% under growth spend. The bridge's 10-15% haircut on the investment book proves too small -- each further 10% haircut on the S$18.3bn REIB carrying value costs ~S$0.36/share, which this scenario does not include.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default) because the REIB leg is held at one haircut across all scenarios and its downside -- further China write-downs and discounted divestments -- lives only in the weighting. Base 50% as the FUM trajectory has tracked ~S$9bn/yr since listing. Bull 25% (below 35%) because it needs fundraising, Ascott pipeline conversion and China recycling to all go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sum of parts. The fee business is the asset the market should eventually pay a manager multiple for; it is valued on owner FCF with SBC expensed. The investment book is not a cash-flow stream to project -- it is a portfolio of mostly listed sponsor stakes and China-heavy property marked at a discount to book, consistent with recent divestment pricing. Consolidated net debt (incl. leases) and NCI are deducted once. Reported PATMI is dominated by revaluation and portfolio-gain noise and is not used.
key_risks_to_valuation: REIB haircut: the S$18.3bn associates/JVs/IP carrying value dominates the bridge; each 10% haircut change is ~S$0.36/share
China: ~two-thirds of the S$7-9bn non-core pool is in China, where divestments have cleared 13-20% below book
Event-driven fees: H1 2026 FRB revenue (+18%) included an India performance fee and divestment/acquisition fees that may not recur
Gearing: net debt/equity rose 0.35x -> 0.43x -> 0.45x while recycling lagged
Ticker collision: Yahoo C09.SI is City Developments; any automated price refresh on C09.SI writes CDL's price into this file

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, symbol 9CI.SI (CapitaLand Investment), at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.29-3.18. Yahoo C09.SI is City Developments and must not be used.
data_sources.financials: C09.SI_Annual_FY2025.txt (financial highlights, note 36 operating segments) and C09.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (balance sheet, note 4 segments, net debt note, note 17(b) diluted shares, note 19 NAV); Metrics.csv FY2021+ only
